title: Reject bare CR near the parallel CSV data boundary
answers: Why does read_csv silently drop the first data row?
Why does parallel CSV reading add a junk first row after a quoted multiline header?
When should bare carriage returns trigger serial CSV fallback?
body:
Symptom: Parallel read_csv silently drops the first data row or adds a junk first row when a bare CR occurs before the data boundary.
Root cause: pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:_read_csv_chunks uses an LF-based data-start offset, but the tokenizer also ends lines at bare CR; the row-count check can miss the mismatch with blank lines or quoted multiline headers.
Fix pattern: Before trusting the boundary, inspect the preamble plus first data line, remove CRLF pairs, and return None from _read_csv_chunks if any CR remains so reading falls back to serial.
Constraints: Apply this guard to the parallel path's preamble and first data line, including skipped rows; preserve CRLF eligibility. This guard does not validate line endings throughout the remaining file.
applies: Parallel read_csv chunk-boundary validation for large local files, including headers, skipped rows, and the first data line.
